content.overview: Specialist instruction for rooting progress, failure localization & evidence within controlled clonal-propagation systems.

sections.title: Separate survival from root formation
sections.body: Turgid leaves show that a cutting has not visibly collapsed, but they do not prove that adventitious roots have formed. Rooting assessment should distinguish early survival, root initiation and usable root development.

sections.title: Locate the failure stage before changing the protocol
sections.body: Loss before root initiation suggests a different problem set from roots that form but fail during later development or transplant. Recording the stage at which loss occurs narrows the next useful checks.

sections.title: Compare batches without overclaiming cause
sections.body: Differences among donors, genotypes, operators, tray positions and dates can reveal patterns, but a pattern is not proof of cause. Strong troubleshooting records preserve plausible alternatives and identify the next discriminating observation or controlled test.

commonMistakes: Calling a cutting rooted based only on leaf appearance.
Changing multiple variables before locating the failure stage.
Treating one failed tray as proof of a universal protocol defect.
content.practicalApplication: Classify a set of propagation failures as pre-root survival, root-initiation, root-development or post-root transition failures and choose the next useful evidence for each.
content.summary: Failure localization turns vague low success into a testable question about where the propagation process is breaking down.
